id1.description: Recording the presence of a harmful or undesirable response to an agent or substance including food, as determined by the clinician - excluding poisoning and abnormal use

id4.description: The agent or substance or class that caused the adverse reaction.

id5.description: Degree of certainty that the agent was the cause of the reaction.

at6.description: A reaction to the agent is deemed to be or have been present by the clinician.

at7.description: The reaction is deemed to be the probable cause of the reaction.

at8.description: The agent is deemed to be a possible cause of the reaction.

at12.description: A substance taken as part of the diet.

at13.description: A living organism or its venom or produce.

at14.description: A substance taken or applied  for medicinal purposes.

id16.description: The type of reaction experience by the person as determined by the clinician.

at17.description: Leads to unpleasant symptoms which are sufficient to avoid use in the future.

at18.description: Leads to morbidity which is potentially threatening to the wellbeing of the person.

at19.description: Leads to an IgE mediated reaction.

id20.description: Details of the reaction experienced by the person.

id21.description: The date (+/- time) when the person became exposed to the agent.

id22.description: The duration of the exposure to the agent.

id23.description: A description of the reaction to this agent as experienced by the person.

at25.description: A reaction which causes little distress and no loss of work/school.

at26.description: A reaction which causes morbidity and/or loss of function.

at27.description: A reaction which was or could be lifethreatening.

at31.description: Person has been exposed with no reaction.

at32.description: A non-medicinal ingredient of medication such as colouring, preservative, etc.(subtype of other chemical)

id33.description: The specific substance that caused the reaction if different from the agent (e.g. brands or members of a class).

at34.description: A dye or media used in diagnostic imaging (subtype of other chemical).

at35.description: An agent present in the environment.

ac2.description: The type of reaction experience by the person as determined by the clinician. (synthesised)

ac3.description: Degree of certainty that the agent was the cause of the reaction. (synthesised)
